max_tire.note: Toyota-4Runner.org owners run 31s with no lift and no regear; 33x12.50s rub the front valance, wheel-well corners and rear pinch weld
IH8MUD: 'about an inch and a half' of lift plus hammering the pinch weld/valance; a narrower 33x10.50 rubs less. Owners call stock gearing 'a dog' on 33s

items.title: Fuel hose too close to EGR pipe
items.summary: Improperly routed fuel hose could lack clearance to the EGR pipe.

items.title: Steering relay rod fatigue crack
items.summary: Repeated full-lock steering under high effort (e.g. parked) can crack the steering relay rod.

timeline.change: US sales start May 1984: two doors, removable fibreglass top, carbureted 22R, five-speed, solid front axle; base DX has no rear seat

Fuel-injected 22R-E (116 hp) arrives; rear seat available on all trims. Last year of the solid front axle, which Hagerty says purists still seek out; an Expedition Portal member rates carbureted trucks less desirable
Hi-Trac independent front suspension replaces the solid axle, track 3 in wider; 22R-TE turbo (135 hp) added
3.0 3VZ-E V6 (145 hp) replaces the turbo on SR5; SR5 gets automatic locking hubs
3.0 3VZ-E V6 trucks: a Hagerty expert says most enthusiasts avoid the six and choose the four, and the 3VZ-E's head-gasket history starts here
Minor cosmetic and option changes before the 1990 replacement

identify.intro: The 1984½–89 trucks look alike but split hard on axle and engine, and the front half is pure Hilux pickup, so check the hardware rather than the badges.

items.head: Solid axle or IFS
items.body: 1984–85 trucks have a solid front axle on leaf springs; 1986–89 have independent front suspension with a 3 in wider track. Look under the front: a beam axle and leaf packs vs torsion bars and CV shafts.

items.head: Engine by year
items.body: 1984½ is carbureted 22R only; EFI 22R-E from 1985; the 22R-TE turbo only for 1986–87, mostly with the automatic; the 3VZ-E V6 for 1988–89 on SR5.

items.head: Rear seat and trim
items.body: Many 1984–86 trucks came in without a rear seat (base DX omitted it), partly to classify them as trucks for import duty. The SR5 package added gauges, better trim and the rear seat.

items.head: Hilux Surf twins
items.body: Japan's Hilux Surf used 3Y petrol and 2L / 2L-T diesel engines that were never sold in the US; a diesel or right-hand-drive 'first gen' is a gray import, not a US 4Runner.

values.intro: Values have climbed hard; clean, unmodified early solid-axle trucks with manual gearboxes take the big money, while IFS automatics stay affordable.
values.note: Based on 20 Bring a Trailer sales from November 2025 to October 2026 (median about $16,600). The top three were 1984–85 solid-axle five-speeds, including a 42k-mile 1985 SR5 at $60,500.

paragraphs: Japan's version was the Hilux Surf (N60), offered with a 2.0 3Y petrol or 2.4 2L diesel and later the 2L-T turbo-diesel, none of them sold in the US. Every one is now well past the US 25-year exemption from federal safety standards, so diesel and right-hand-drive Surfs can come in, but state titling and emissions rules still apply and vary.

production.intro: Built at Tahara, Japan, from October 1983 to August 1989; US sales took off only once the V6 arrived.
